chapter: Teddy Wilson bands and Cafe Society
title: Teddy Wilson's sextet at Cafe Society and the Frank Fairfax band
summary: Hall names the sextet members, Jimmy Hamilton, and Philadelphian players from the Frank Fairfax band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: We went to Cafe Society in 1940.
Yeah. Who was in that?
Bill Coleman, my greatest buddy, and Benny Morton and Jim Hamilton, Yank Porter was the original drummer --
And who came in on drums then?
J. C.
J. C. Heard?
J. C. Heard came in.
Jimmy Hamilton was in Philadelphia.
Yeah, well, he wasn't from Philadelphia, but --
He had played around there. We were in the Boy Scouts together at age ten, but he was an upright horn player.
Yeah, I know that from Dizzy because Dizzy worked with him in the Frank Fairfax band
and he said he called him "Joe Trumpet" and he still calls him "Joe Trumpet."
Right, right.
That was his nickname for him.
Yeah. And Charlie Shavers was there too.
And Carl Warwick.

Yeah. But Frank Fairfax had the big band that he took over from Chappie Willett. [Rawfield, west] They were a black college band from Virginia that came to Philadelphia and Chappie Willett was the ace arranger at that point and got the band together, but there wasn't any work for a big band. There wasn't any work for seven day, six day basis for music in Philadelphia, period.
Yeah.

So, the guys either split or stayed there and deteriorated. You got your day job and you go to the post office or the police force or fireman, and you would just stay there and grow old. So those that left were called adventurous. I left. (Laughter)
But it's interesting that so many of the people from that band, the Frank Fairfax band did go on to all those names we just named.
Yeah. And Joe Wiler's dad was a bass player. Curtis Wiler. And I knew Joe when he was a baby.
One of the finest musicians there is. Bar none.
